about: The lords2 work ledger: every piece of work that is in flight, waiting, or known and not started. It is the project's memory of what is left, and the lead is its interface. Rules: (1) the lead writes or updates a row BEFORE dispatching an agent and BEFORE replying to an agent's report; (2) rows store INTENT only - what, why, source, dependencies, next step; (3) anything git can answer (merged, commits ahead of main, HANDOFF.md present) is DERIVED by tooling from the row's branch and must never be typed here; (4) merged work leaves this file - git log is the record of what landed. Keyed by id for the keyed merge driver.

states.in-flight: an agent is working on it now
states.queued-merge: finished on its branch and handed to the integrator
states.awaiting-user: cannot move until the player or owner decides or observes something
states.deferred: deliberately not being done now, with the reason in note
states.abandoned: will not be done; the reason is in note

tracks.play: a game plays start to finish: turns, economy, armies, battle, sieges, AI, winning and losing
tracks.screens: every screen and control behaves as the original: input kinds, draws, strings, fonts
tracks.instruments: the checks that prove parity rather than assert it

The integrator names them as one class: --assign writing the worktree while the commit takes the index, --relock making corrections.js --check green for whoever runs it after the edit, and the features schema enforced in both work.js --check and work_ledger.rs so a 42-character gap was caught by the test and not the tool. items.title: The census is the one file where a clean merge misleads
items.source: integrator on C202: both sides took GATED_TOTAL from 522 to 526 by different rows, so git saw the constant agree, kept it, and applied both inventories underneath; the true total was 530. Every other merge in the run conflicted on that line and forced a recount
items.next: make the constant derived rather than stored, or make the census test the only place it is written, so a merge cannot agree on a number while disagreeing on what it counts
items.note: the census test would catch it, but only after a full suite run and only if nobody read the clean merge as a settled number | C203 confirmed the mechanism from the other side: the census prints a correct INVENTORY when the list disagrees but asserts the total in a separate statement, so a total wrong by a constant survives every run that does not touch the list. The branch's 537 was a typed number; the count is 541
